title: Faith does not justify by its own merit or dignity
source_text: VII. Nec minus inter eos constat fidem nos non justificare, aut justitiam nobis a Deo impetrare, proprio merito atque dignitate. Quamvis enim divinae bonitati congruum & consentaneum sit, ut in gratiam recipiat credentem & resipiscentem, ac omnino polliceatur summa Dei aequitas atque sapientia, ut peccata condonet, potius peccatori per fidem & poenitentiam ad misericordiam ipsius confugienti, quam impoenitenti atque incredulo qui divinam gratiam respuit atque contemnit: ex justitia tamen non tenetur Deus credenti peccata remittere, illumque justitiae Christi participem facere, & acceptare ad vitam aeternam. Quodque Deus erga credentem ita benigne & paterne se gerit, ad meram ejus gratiam & misericordiam omnino referendum est. Quod Scriptura frequenter & evidenter docet, dum pluribus in locis inculcat, nos justificari gratis, secundum gratiam, non secundum debitum, praesertim vero tertio, & quarto capite epistolae ad Rom. Nam, si fides mereretur justificationem, justificatio gratuita non esset, & non ex mera gratia, sed ex debito justificaremur.
pass_a_gloss: Nor less is it agreed among them that faith does not justify us, or obtain righteousness for us from God, by its own proper merit and dignity. For although it is congruent and agreeable to divine goodness that he receive the believer and the repentant into grace, and God's supreme equity and wisdom altogether promise that he rather forgives sins to the sinner who by faith and repentance flees to his mercy than to the impenitent and unbelieving who spurns and despises divine grace: yet God is not bound by justice to remit sins to the believer, make him a partaker of Christ's righteousness, and accept him to eternal life. And that God so kindly and fatherly deals with the believer is to be referred entirely to his mere grace and mercy. Which Scripture frequently and evidently teaches when in many places it presses that we are justified freely, according to grace, not according to debt—especially in Romans chapters 3 and 4. For if faith merited justification, justification would not be free, and we would be justified not from mere grace but from debt.
pass_b_english: Faith does not justify by its own merit; grace alone binds God to the believer.
If faith earned justification, it would be debt not free grace (Rom 3–4).

lemmas.gloss: by its own merit and dignity
according to grace, not according to debt

choices.why: Fitting to goodness, not owed by justice.
